summary: Create a small `board` capability because cross-capability filtering, grouping, label projection, and rejection policy belong together. Work-items and labels remain independent and are consumed only through trusted server APIs.

tree.purpose: Orchestrates reads and owns board policy: hide archived items, group by status, attach visible labels, and reject inaccessible labels.
Defines minimal board-specific reader ports for work-items and actor-visible labels.
Server-only RSC surface; authenticates the request, constructs identity/effects, invokes `load-board`, and maps unexpected failures to reporting/error-boundary behavior.
RSC route that calls `board/rsc.ts` and renders the resulting board model.
Existing trusted work-item read API; owns persistence, tenant/ownership predicates, and row mapping.
Existing trusted label read API; owns persistence and actor visibility authorization.
Reusable board presentation only if needed outside the route; otherwise keep presentation under the route.
Tests board policy and typed expected outcomes using ports.
Tests RSC integration, auth behavior, and rendering outcomes.

flows: `load-board.ts` → `work-items/server.ts` to read scoped work-items including status → exclude archived items → group remaining items by status.

`load-board.ts` → collect label IDs from retained items → `labels/server.ts` with actor identity → attach returned visible label details; if any referenced label is rejected, return a typed inaccessible-label outcome.
`board/rsc.ts` maps expected outcomes to page-level not-found/forbidden states and reports an unexpected exception once before delegating to the RSC error boundary.

decisions.rationale: Removing it would move meaningful board policy into the page or make work-items own label concerns.

decisions.choice: Board depends on narrow ports wired to `work-items/server.ts` and `labels/server.ts`
decisions.rationale: The two existing capabilities never import each other and remain independently changeable.
Hiding archived items is board-specific policy.

decisions.choice: Require an explicit visible/rejected result from the labels API
decisions.rationale: Silent omission cannot distinguish an inaccessible label from missing data.
This task requires an RSC read; no actions, HTTP handlers, streams, jobs, or browser API are required.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at `board/rsc.ts`; enforce board policy in the application; enforce tenant/ownership and label visibility at stores
decisions.rationale: Each boundary enforces the authorization it owns.

decisions.choice: Typed expected outcomes for access/rejection; exceptions for unexpected outages, reported once at the RSC boundary
decisions.rationale: Preserves RSC-native error handling and avoids duplicate reporting.

risks: The work-items read contract must expose status; otherwise the board cannot reliably apply its archived-item policy.
Labels must explicitly identify rejected IDs or return a typed authorization failure.
UI and route code must not import `server.ts`, `rsc.ts`, or private server directories from the browser; enforce this with `server-only`/`client-only` boundaries and a production build check.
